locations.name: Old Town Lanes
locations.description: Narrow lanes behind the wholesale market, where things fall off lorries and nobody asks questions. 18+, mature themes.

locations.name: Lucky Star Club
locations.description: Card tables, a roulette wheel, slot machines and a betting desk for every match. The house always wins — eventually.

locations.name: City Police Station
locations.description: A busy station with a front desk, a lock-up and a community-policing notice board.

actions.label: Pick pockets in the market crowd
actions.description: Quick hands, crowded buses, distracted shoppers. Small money, small risk — at first.

then.label: Pick pockets in the market crowd

actions.label: Shoplift from a crowded store
actions.description: Earphones and perfume slip into a bag. The cameras might be fake.

actions.label: Sell fake branded goods
actions.description: A tarpaulin, a pile of "designer" handbags and an eye on the street corner.

actions.label: Carry a 'no-questions' package
actions.description: Pappu Bhai needs something taken across town. Don’t open it. Don’t get stopped.

actions.label: Steal a car to order
actions.description: A buyer wants a particular SUV. You know where one sleeps.

actions.label: Burgle an empty bungalow
actions.description: The family is abroad for a month. The neighbours are not.

actions.label: Lie low for a few days
actions.description: Stay off the streets, change your routes, let things cool down.

actions.label: Ask around about Pappu Bhai's crew
actions.description: Word is the man who runs these lanes is always recruiting.

actions.label: Plan the bank-vault job
actions.description: The crew has a blueprint, a guard on the payroll and a date. They need a planner.

actions.label: Join an armed bank robbery
actions.description: A crew wants you on lookout while a masked robbery unfolds. Guns, alarms and panic mean this can ruin a life fast.

actions.label: Get pulled into a kidnapping plot
actions.description: A crew talks about holding a rival's cousin for ransom. You can walk away, warn someone, or cross a line.

actions.label: Turn yourself in and confess
actions.description: Walk up to the front desk and tell them everything. It might be the bravest thing you do.

effects.title: Came clean
effects.text: You confessed at the police station. A record, a fine, and a strange lightness.

actions.label: Rehabilitation & community service
actions.description: Sweep parks, mentor kids from your lane, sit with a probation counsellor. Six sessions.

then.title: A clean slate
then.text: Six months of community service. The court has sealed your record. People look at you differently now — and so do you.

actions.label: Volunteer as a community warden
actions.description: Traffic duty at the school gate and night walks with the beat constable.

actions.label: Report what you know about the lanes
actions.description: An anonymous tip about the stolen-goods racket behind the market.

actions.label: Buy a lottery ticket
actions.description: ₹100 for a dream. The odds are printed very small on the back.

actions.label: Bet ₹2,000 on tonight's cricket match
actions.description: Even money on the home side. You know cricket — right?

then.label: Bet ₹2,000 on tonight's cricket match: winnings

actions.label: Roulette: ₹5,000 on red
actions.description: The wheel spins. Eighteen red, eighteen black — and one green zero for the house.

actions.label: Play the slot machines (₹1,000)
actions.description: Lights, sounds and the feeling you are always almost winning.

actions.label: Back a long shot at the races (₹3,000)
actions.description: Moonlight Express at 5 to 1. The tipster swears by her.

then.label: Back a long shot at the races (₹3,000): winnings

actions.label: Teen patti night (₹10,000 buy-in)
actions.description: Cards, chai and men who talk too much when they bluff. Street smarts help here.

actions.label: High-roller baccarat (₹1,00,000)
actions.description: A private room, a dealer in a waistcoat and the biggest single bet of your life.

actions.label: Borrow ₹50,000 from Shetty
actions.description: Shetty lends to anyone at the club. Repayment in thirty days: ₹75,000. He's never been paid late twice.

actions.label: Ask the club to ban you for good
actions.description: Sign the self-exclusion register. The bouncers will turn you away from now on.

effects.title: Walked away
effects.text: You signed the self-exclusion register at the Lucky Star Club. No more bets.

actions.label: Gambling addiction counselling
actions.description: Group sessions with people who lost far more than money. Four sessions.

then.title: Free of it
then.text: Four sessions, many urges resisted. Gambling no longer runs your life.

puzzles.prompt: The take is three bundles of a hundred ₹500 notes and two bundles of a hundred ₹200 notes. How much in total (₹)?
The guard changes every 45 minutes starting at 9:00 p.m. Which of these times is NOT a shift change?
puzzles.explanation: Changes fall at 9:00, 9:45, 10:30, 11:15, 12:00… 11:00 is not one of them.

puzzles.prompt: Five people split ₹8,00,000. The planner takes 30% and the rest is shared equally among the other four. How much does each of the four get (₹)?
puzzles.explanation: The planner takes ₹2,40,000. The remaining ₹5,60,000 ÷ 4 = ₹1,40,000 each.

puzzles.prompt: A new crew member brags loudly about the job in a tea shop. What is the safest move?
options: Pull them out quietly and call off anything they knew about
Shout at them in the shop
puzzles.explanation: Loose talk is how jobs are lost. Quietly limit the damage and change what they knew.

puzzles.prompt: Three exits: A is watched every night, B on even dates only, C on odd dates only. Tonight is the 14th. Which exit is unwatched?
puzzles.explanation: The 14th is even: A and B are watched. C is watched only on odd dates, so it is clear tonight.

puzzles.prompt: You buy stolen phones at ₹4,000 and sell at ₹6,500. Profit on 12 phones (₹)?

careers.name: Member of Pappu Bhai's crew
careers.description: Collections, deliveries and jobs you do not talk about. The money is real; so are the police raids and the rivals.

events.title: Caught
events.summary: The police catch up with you.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A hand on your shoulder. "Come with us." The constable is younger than you, and very pleased.

choices.label: Plead guilty and pay the fine (₹5,000).
Accept the charge and serve the sentence (thirty days in the district jail).
choices.hint: Time passes while you are inside.

fined.speaker: narrator
fined.text: You pay at the counter, sign three forms and walk out with a record in the computer and a lecture in your ears.

bribe_ok.speaker: narrator
bribe_ok.text: The officer counts it without looking at you. The paperwork goes missing. You tell yourself it was smart.

bribe_fail.speaker: narrator
bribe_fail.text: Wrong officer. He photographs the cash as evidence and adds a second charge.

choices.label: There is nothing left to do but serve the time.

acquitted.speaker: narrator
acquitted.text: Your lawyer takes the case apart, piece by piece. The judge acquits you. Outside the court, you breathe for the first time in weeks.

convicted.speaker: narrator
convicted.text: Thirty days in the district jail. You learn the rhythms of the place: roll call, meals, the one hour of sky.

onEnter.title: Prison
onEnter.text: Thirty days in the district jail. The days are long and the nights are longer.

released.speaker: narrator
released.text: The gate opens. The city has moved on without you. Whatever you do next is up to you — and it doesn't have to be this.

events.title: Arrested
events.summary: The police catch up with you.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: They come at dawn. Two jeeps, one warrant, and a neighbour filming from a balcony.

choices.label: Accept the charge and serve the sentence (a year in prison).
choices.hint: Time passes while you are inside.

bribe_ok.speaker: narrator
bribe_ok.text: The officer counts it without looking at you. The paperwork goes missing. You tell yourself it was smart.

convicted.text: A year in prison. You learn the rhythms of the place: roll call, meals, the one hour of sky.

events.title: The Big Arrest
events.summary: The police catch up with you.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The heist is on every news channel, and now so is your face.

choices.label: Accept the charge and serve the sentence (three years in prison).
choices.hint: Time passes while you are inside.

bribe_ok.speaker: narrator
bribe_ok.text: The officer counts it without looking at you. The paperwork goes missing. You tell yourself it was smart.

bribe_fail.speaker: narrator
bribe_fail.text: Wrong officer. He photographs the cash as evidence and adds a second charge.

choices.label: There is nothing left to do but serve the time.

acquitted.speaker: narrator
acquitted.text: Your lawyer takes the case apart, piece by piece. The judge acquits you. Outside the court, you breathe for the first time in weeks.

convicted.text: Three years in prison. You learn the rhythms of the place: roll call, meals, the one hour of sky.

events.title: Pappu Bhai
events.summary: The man who runs the lanes wants to meet you.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A back room above a mobile-repair shop. Pappu Bhai is smaller than you imagined, and much calmer. 'I hear you're sharp,' he says. 'I pay sharp people well. Weekly, in cash.'

choices.label: Keep your life as it is, but take the odd job.

joined.speaker: narrator
joined.text: He shakes your hand. 'Runners first. Everyone starts as a runner.'

side.speaker: narrator
side.text: 'Freelancers,' he sighs. 'Fine. When the big job comes, you'll hear from us.'

refused.speaker: narrator
refused.text: He shrugs. 'The door stays open.' On the stairs, your heart is pounding — and you're glad.

events.title: The Vault Job
events.summary: The biggest job the crew has ever tried.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Blueprints on a carrom board. A guard schedule. A getaway route through the old market. Everyone is looking at you.

choices.label: Back out. This is too far.

success.speaker: narrator
success.text: Four minutes inside. Nobody hurt. Your share is in a gym bag under your bed and you cannot sleep.

onEnter.label: Your share of the vault job

empty.speaker: narrator
empty.text: The alarm trips early. You run with nothing, but you run clean.

caught.speaker: narrator
caught.text: Sirens before you even reach the vault. Somebody talked.

events.title: Alarms at Kaveri Bank
events.summary: An armed robbery explodes into sirens and panic.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The bank lobby freezes. A weapon flashes under fluorescent lights, someone screams, and the alarm starts its thin, terrible song.

effects.title: Ran from the robbery
effects.text: You ran from an armed robbery before it turned worse.

choices.label: Hold your nerve and follow the crew.
Help people get down and call the police.

ran.speaker: narrator
ran.text: You make it two lanes away before your legs stop shaking. Behind you, sirens fold into the evening traffic.

shootout.speaker: narrator
shootout.text: A shot cracks. Glass jumps. Nobody feels brave anymore.

escape.speaker: narrator
escape.text: You escape with cash and a sound in your memory you cannot wash out. Every police jeep looks slower until it looks directly at you.

caught.speaker: narrator
caught.text: The city locks down faster than the crew expected. By midnight, your name is in a file.

helped.speaker: narrator
helped.text: You keep strangers calm until the police arrive. One old man grips your hand like you are the only solid thing in the room.

events.title: The Ransom Call
events.summary: A kidnapping plot forces a choice.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The plan is uglier when said aloud: hold someone, frighten a family, collect money. The room waits to see who you are.

choices.label: Tip off the family and the police.

refused.speaker: narrator
refused.text: They laugh when you leave. The laugh bothers you less than the fact that you almost stayed.

warned.speaker: narrator
warned.text: The family disappears for a week. The crew knows somebody talked. Old Town feels smaller after that.

fallout.speaker: narrator
fallout.text: Ransom money changes hands, then so do phone records, CCTV clips and rumours. This is not a secret. It is a fuse.

choices.label: Take the money and disappear for a while.

paid.speaker: narrator
paid.text: The person is released alive. Your share of the money arrives wrapped in newspaper. It feels heavier than it is.

caught.speaker: narrator
caught.text: Kidnapping turns every phone tower into a witness. The police arrive before dawn.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Two large men are waiting at your gate. 'Shetty says hello. Shetty says seventy-five thousand.'

choices.label: Pay whatever you have, and owe the rest.
Go to the police and file a complaint.
Offer to "work it off" for Shetty.

paid.speaker: narrator
paid.text: They count it on the bonnet of your neighbour’s car. "Pleasure doing business." Any shortfall is now overdue — and Shetty knows where you live.

police.speaker: narrator
police.text: The inspector takes it seriously. Shetty’s club is raided a week later; the debt quietly disappears. You still check the gate at night.

work.speaker: narrator
work.text: You spend a month doing collections for Shetty. You are good at it, which frightens you.

beaten.speaker: narrator
beaten.text: You wake up in a hospital bed. The money is gone from your account. Some lessons cost more than ₹75,000.

achievements.title: Beat the House
achievements.description: Won big at the Lucky Star Club.

achievements.title: Kingpin
achievements.description: Rose to the top of the crew.

achievements.title: Clean Slate
achievements.description: Completed rehabilitation and had your record sealed.

conclusions.title: The Lanes
conclusions.text: The brochures never mentioned this path. You run errands for a man who pays in cash and never writes anything down. The money is better than your friends' starting salaries; the fear is worse than any exam. Every chapter after this one can still turn — people walk out of the lanes every year. The question is whether you will.

epilogueLines.text: A police record follows you into the next chapter. Some doors are harder to open now — but rehabilitation can seal it.
The club still calls to you at night. Counselling at the hospital has helped others walk away.
